title: Paediatric body and neuroimaging

steps.tx: Neonatal gastrointestinal emergencies require standardized ultrasonographic assessment. **Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis** is diagnosed on ultrasound by a **pyloric muscle thickness** >= 3.0 mm (single wall) and pyloric canal length >= 14 mm in infants presenting with non-bilious projectile vomiting between 2 and 8 weeks of age.
steps.say: Neonatal gastrointestinal emergencies require standardized ultrasonographic assessment. Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis is diagnosed on ultrasound by a pyloric muscle thickness at least 3.0 mm single wall and pyloric canal length at least 14 mm in infants presenting with non-bilious projectile vomiting between 2 and 8 weeks of age.

steps.tx: Acute paediatric bowel invaginations demonstrate classic ultrasonographic patterns. **Intussusception** in infants typically presents with the target sign or **doughnut sign** in transverse ultrasound and the pseudokidney sign in longitudinal plane, successfully reduced in over 80% to 90% by air or hydrostatic contrast enema under fluoroscopic or sonographic guidance.

steps.tx: Embryonic midgut rotation abnormalities present as catastrophic surgical emergencies. **Midgut volvulus** secondary to intestinal malrotation classically produces the **corkscrew sign** of the redundant twisted duodenum and proximal jejunum on upper GI contrast series, with color Doppler demonstrating the whirlpool sign (clockwise wrapping of SMV around SMA).

steps.tx: Premature neonatal gastrointestinal distress requires close radiologic surveillance in intensive care nurseries. **Necrotizing enterocolitis** (NEC) on abdominal radiographs demonstrates **pneumatosis intestinalis** (pathognomonic intramural gas), portal venous gas (branching tubular gas extending to the liver periphery), and pneumoperitoneum indicating intestinal perforation.

steps.tx: Paediatric abdominal masses require accurate cross-sectional origin determination. **Wilms tumour** (nephroblastoma) is an intrarenal solid mass that expands within the renal parenchyma, distorting the pyelocaliceal system and producing the **claw sign** of splayed normal renal parenchyma, typically presenting between 2 and 5 years of age.

steps.tx: Neural crest malignancies exhibit distinctive invasive calcifying behaviours. **Neuroblastoma** arises from the adrenal medulla or sympathetic chain, characteristically demonstrating coarse intratumoural calcifications (90% on CT), **encasing great vessels** (aorta, IVC, celiac axis) without vascular invasion, and displacing the kidney inferolaterally.

vis.caption: Neuroblastoma: adrenal primary encasing great vessels with extensive calcifications (StewardMD).

steps.tx: Congenital diaphragmatic malformations manifest with thoracic herniation of abdominal organs. **Congenital diaphragmatic hernia** most frequently occurs through the posterolateral **foramen of Bochdalek** (85% on the left), presenting on chest radiograph with multiple air-filled loops of bowel in the hemithorax, mediastinal shift, and a scaphoid abdomen.

steps.tx: Congenital posterior fossa malformations display characteristic cerebellar vermian dysgenesis. **Dandy-Walker malformation** is characterized by the triad of complete or partial **agenesis of the cerebellar vermis**, cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle filling the posterior fossa, and an elevated tentorium with high torcula (torcular-lambdoid inversion).
